hypotheses.reasoning: order-consumer hits a RangeError (call stack overflow in expandReferences) while processing msg-329298 at orders.events offset 442796. The consumer does not skip or dead-letter it: after each restart it resumes at the same committed offset 442796 (#752, #774, #827) and crashes again (#755, #778). This is a crash loop on one malformed message, which explains CrashLoopBackOff and the growing orders.events lag, since the consumer makes no progress past that offset. Earlier batches are healthy, and the failure is per-message and deterministic rather than load-driven. Other services show no errors. The report-cron ModuleNotFoundError (pandas, image report-cron:2026.10.2, #236 onward) is a separate, unrelated failure.

A stack overflow could in principle come from runaway recursion or a resource limit, but the failure is deterministic for one message at one offset, not load-driven. Order-service GC and heap look healthy (#728), so this is unlikely.

verdict.recommendedAction: Dead-letter or skip the poison message msg-329298 at orders.events offset 442796 (advance the consumer group offset past it) so order-consumer can resume. Then inspect that payload for deeply nested or self-referencing references, and add a depth guard or DLQ handling in expandReferences. Separately, fix report-cron by installing pandas in image report-cron:2026.10.2 or rolling back to the prior image; it is unrelated to this incident.
